A big way to judge how well money will be spent is "Does the money come from the people/organization, or does it come from a guaranteed outside source?" and "Are they buying for themselves, or for someone else?"

When someone is spending their own money on themselves, they care a lot about both cost and quality. (Example: small corporations trying to hire the best staff and purchase the best equipment that their budget can afford)

When someone is spending their own money on others, they solely care about cost, with no regard for quality. (Example: birthday party guests getting cheap little gifts that are almost guaranteed to break within the next year)

When someone is spending other people's money on themselves, they solely care about quality, and write off any excess cost. (Example: executives at big corporations charging the company account for the penthouse suite and limousine service at their yearly retreat)

When someone is spending other people's money on others, they no longer have any incentive to care about cost or quality. (Example: career politicians who know that they have access to a million-dollar fund that is earmarked for "disaster relief in Haiti", but also have a million-dollar bill they need to pay for their daughter's wedding, and decide to save money out of their own pocketbook by using the government funds and lying that it was used in Haiti)
